name: Vietnamese Thit Kho Braised Pork and Eggs
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Caramel braise with hard-boiled eggs stirred in, which pushes protein up cheaply. Distinct from both live Vietnamese pork entries (those are grilled lemongrass chops and bun bowls). Source publishes 1,128 cal / 28g protein per serving at a 50/50 belly-shoulder ratio; going all pork shoulder cuts calories hard and lifts protein. Coconut soda swaps to tracked coconut milk plus sugar. | HARVEST: Published nutrition covers the braise only; rice served alongside is not included.
OVERRIDE Zero-Sugar Soda: splitter split '6 fl oz Rico coconut soda'
intro_html: Thit kho is the dish Vietnamese families make for Tet and then eat happily for the next week, because it holds beautifully and the flavor deepens every day. Pork braised in a dark caramel with fish sauce, with hard boiled eggs sitting in the pot soaking it all up. Going all pork shoulder instead of belly pushes it to 47 grams of protein for about $1.89 a bowl.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.27. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $26.50 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.89 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $29.25 across 14 servings, roughly $2.09 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $9.12 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $38.37. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $1.89 a bowl for a caramel braise with eggs already in it. This is one of the highest protein plates in the entire library and it is nowhere near the most expensive.
shop_smart: Pork shoulder instead of belly is the whole trick. The traditional build is half belly, which is mostly fat at a premium price. Shoulder braises just as tender and the protein number jumps.
Eggs are how you get protein for almost nothing. They braise right in the pot, take on the color and the flavor, and cost a fraction of what more meat would.

Soda stands in for coconut soda. The traditional recipe uses a coconut soda that is hard to find outside an Asian market. Plain soda with the sugar in this recipe does the same job of building the caramel.
Fish sauce is not optional and one bottle lasts a year. There is no substitute for it here. Buy a decent bottle once and it will carry many batches of this and a dozen other recipes.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork shoulder into large chunks and slice the onion. Hard boil the eggs, cool them and peel them.
Melt the sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat without stirring and let it turn a deep amber caramel. Watch it closely, because caramel goes from amber to burnt in about ten seconds.
Add the pork chunks to the caramel and stir to coat every piece, then add the sliced onion.
Pour in the fish sauce and the soda, which will hiss and seize the caramel at first. Keep stirring and it will loosen back out.
Add enough water to nearly cover the pork, bring it to a simmer, and skim off whatever foam rises in the first few minutes.
Cover and braise very low until the pork is tender and the liquid has reduced into a glossy sauce, stirring occasionally.
Add the peeled eggs for the last stretch so they take on color and flavor, season with salt and black pepper, and cook the rice separately.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and ladle the exact amount over rice in each container, splitting the eggs evenly between them. Every bowl lands near 683 calories with a serious 47 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from hungryhuy.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: High protein braises for about $1.89 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Vietnamese thit kho, pork braised in a fish sauce caramel with hard boiled eggs, served over rice. 14 servings, 683 calories, 47g protein, about $1.89 each.
head.keywords: thit kho, vietnamese braised pork and eggs, caramel braised pork, fish sauce pork, high protein meal prep
steps: Cut the pork shoulder into chunks and hard boil and peel the eggs.
Melt the sugar into a deep amber caramel in a heavy pot without stirring.
Add the pork and sliced onion to the caramel and stir to coat.
Pour in the fish sauce and soda, add water to nearly cover, and skim the foam.
Braise covered on low until tender, add the peeled eggs near the end, and serve over rice.
